name: Environmental perception of public space – Hong Kong (12 space types)
description: Faithful replication of Ho & Au (2020, Frontiers in Psychology), who built a scale for how people perceive public spaces. Each participant sees one of 12 Hong Kong public spaces (transport facility, street, square, recreational space, found neighbourhood space, park, memorial, market, playground, community open space, indoor marketplace, waterfront), shown with the definition of its space type, and rates it on the retained scale items: 8 affective word pairs (comfort, activity), 22 cognitive statements (legibility, enclosure, complexity, crime potential, wildlife, lighting) and 12 outcome statements (perceived restorativeness, safety, visitability), all 1–7. Images: the 12 photographs printed in the paper's Figure 1 (CC BY 4.0), cut from the figure, so they are small (about 320 px wide, shown enlarged). Differences from the original study: (1) the first step, where participants saw all 12 pictures before rating one, is left out; (2) the 26 extra items collected for another purpose and the items the authors dropped are not included. The template is taken down if the authors object.

Each participant is shown one of 12 Hong Kong public spaces (one per space type, with its definition) and rates it on the retained items of the scale: 8 affective word pairs (comfort, activity) and 22 cognitive statements (legibility, enclosure, complexity, crime potential, wildlife, lighting), plus 12 outcome statements (perceived restorativeness, safety, visitability), all on 7-point scales. Images: the 12 photographs printed in the paper's Figure 1 (CC BY 4.0), cut from the figure and therefore small (about 320 px wide, shown enlarged). Differences from the original study: (1) the first step, where participants saw all 12 pictures in random order before rating one, is left out; (2) the 26 extra items the authors collected for another purpose are not included; (3) items from the initial pool that the authors dropped are not included.
